text:
pagerduty: ALERT: GPU node kernel panic detected - rack-09-node-17. Severity: P1. Trigger: node-exporter: kernel_panic_count > 0

oncall-bot: page fired -> assigned to eli (primary on-call). Incident link: https://pd.example/INC123456

eli: acked. Pulling logs now. Will post findings.

maya: noted — any customer-facing latency spikes? Metrics show a small blip in inference throughput in us-west-2 zone.

eli: confirmed 17:03 UTC there's a spike. Affected shards: inference-pool-usw2-gpu-3 (20% error rate increase). We'll cordon and failover.

josh: good plan. If kubelet is dead we should force-drain and spin up replacements. Watch NVMe mounts — we had issues on this rack before.

eli: dumping dmesg from node (excerpt):
```
[  102.345678] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
[  102.345689] CPU: 3 PID: 5678 Comm: kubelet Not tainted 5.10.0
[  102.345701] Call Trace:
[  102.345712]  dump_stack+0x6d/0x8b
[  102.345723]  panic+0x12f/0x2a0
[  102.345734]  ? nvme_completion_is_ok+0x20/0x20
[  102.345745]  nvme_core_cmd_complete+0x1b0/0x2a0
```

priyaa: (typo) priya: NVMe mentions — can hw confirm drive health? @hw-team please check SMART logs for node-17.

hw-team: on it. Pulling SMART. If disks failing we'll RMA.

eli: action plan: 1) mark node unschedulable (cordon), 2) force drain pods with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data, 3) trigger replacement with autoscaler group, 4) attach fallback model variant to impacted routes until capacity restores. Executing step 1 now.

eli: command run:
```
kubectl cordon rack-09-node-17
kubectl drain rack-09-node-17 --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

oncall-bot: drain command issued, 12 pods evicted. Some pods failed to terminate due to stuck local volume. Observability flagged model-serving-pod-724 still pending on node.

josh: I'm taking the drain to manual: delete the stuck pods, they will be recreated on other nodes.

josh: commands:
```
kubectl delete pod model-serving-pod-724 -n inference --force --grace-period=0
```

maya: updating incident page: customer impact currently "partial degradation" for API keys with region=us-west-2. Notifying support and customers with SLA > enterprise.

priyaa: sending customer note draft: "We're investigating elevated errors for inference in US-WEST-2 due to a hardware failure; traffic is failing over to healthy capacity. We'll update in 30m."

eli: HW team reports one NVMe SMART failure on node-17 (Media and Data Integrity errors). They've initiated RMA.

hw-team: SMART output (trimmed):
```
ID#  ATTRIBUTE_NAME          FLAG     VALUE WORST THRESH TYPE      UPDATED  WHEN_FAILED RAW_VALUE
5    Reallocated_Sector_Ct   0x0033   100   100   10   Pre-fail  Always       -       0
199  UDMA_CRC_Error_Count     0x0032   200   200   0    Old_age   Always       -       23
```
Potential link cable or controller flakiness.

eli: replacement node requested. Autoscaler has provisioned replacement instance id: i-0b7efcde. Pods are rescheduling.

oncall-bot: Incident priorities: P1 -> page on-call until resolved. Escalation to engineering manager if not resolved in 30 minutes.

maya: @support FYI — customers with high SLA toggled to route->fallback model. Logs show error rates down to baseline after 6m.

priyaa: adding postmortem stub to internal tracker INC-123456 -> assigned to eli and maya.

eli: marking node as unsalvageable for now. Will coordinate final RMA once replacement validated.

josh: follow-up: add a test in the autoscaler to detect NVMe SMART spikes as a preemptive signal. Filing a JIRA.

maya: thanks team — I'll close the pager once replacement is verified and latency metrics stable for 15m.

oncall-bot: pager acknowledged by eli at 17:10 UTC. Last update: replacement healthy, pod counts normalized.

eli: closing notes: root cause likely NVMe/controller causing kernel panic. Immediate mitigation: cordon+drain+RMA+autoscale fallback. Customer impact: brief partial degradation for US-WEST-2, mitigated within 12 minutes. Postmortem next steps: action items for autoscaler detection and runbook updates.

priyaa: :thumbsup: thanks everyone.

josh: reassigning to maya/eli for postmortem writeup.

oncall-bot: incident thread closed at 17:22 UTC."
